## Ambiguity policy backtest (omit versus hybrid versus guess)

Criterion fixed in advance: step-level F1, then exactly reproduced cases, then fewer extra steps; ties go to the more conservative policy (omit, then hybrid, then guess).

| policy | step F1 | exact cases | extra steps (fp) | missing steps (fn) | status accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| omit | 0.9842 | 26/32 | 0 | 6 | 32/32 |
| hybrid | 0.9895 | 28/32 | 0 | 4 | 32/32 |
| guess | 0.9869 | 28/32 | 1 | 4 | 32/32 |

Winner under the criterion: `hybrid`.

- policy `omit`: guesses made on sample cases: 0, correct: 0; ambiguous accounts left out: 3
- policy `hybrid`: guesses made on sample cases: 2, correct: 2; ambiguous accounts left out: 1
- policy `guess`: guesses made on sample cases: 3, correct: 2; ambiguous accounts left out: 0

Sample size is small, so the margin deserves caution. Across all 540 deletion cases the `guess` policy makes 111 account guesses and 24 analytics guesses; the samples cannot say how accurate those are outside the samples.

## Status/worker-result tiebreak uses

- all cases (samples + eval, matching context): 116 uses, 80 narrowed to one account
- sample cases: 6 uses, 5 narrowed to one account
